title: Local Frobenius and local alternating trace
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\neq p$, $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $Y_0$ be a finite-type $k_0$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], put $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and choose a Weil complex $K=(M,\theta)\in D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,E)$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], so that $M=\operatorname{For}K$ and $\theta:L g_Y^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}M$, where $g_Y=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ and $\gamma=\operatorname{Frob}_q$ is geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Derived pullbacks are those of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $g_s=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$. For a geometric point $\bar x:s\to Y$ [def-weil-geometric-point], write
$$
 K_{\bar x}:=L\bar x^*M,\qquad
 C_{\bar x}:=\operatorname{Fib}_s(K_{\bar x})\in D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E),
$$
where $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ is the rational point-fiber functor [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. The cohomology-sheaf stalk notation $\mathcal H^j(M)_{\bar x}$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] is interpreted at these coefficients as $\mathrm H^j(C_{\bar x})$ [def-weil-coefficient-cohomology-modules]; in particular it is a finite-dimensional $E$-vector space, zero for all but finitely many $j$.

For $n\geq1$ and $x\in Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], use the inclusion $\mathbf F_{q^n}\subset k$ to obtain $\bar x:s\to Y$. Define $\theta^{[1]}=\theta$ and
$$
 \theta^{[n+1]}=\theta^{[n]}\circ L(g_Y^n)^*(\theta):
 L(g_Y^{n+1})^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}M.
$$
Here and below use the canonical pullback-composition comparisons: at finite coefficient level they are those of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], at integral level the comparisons of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] for the integral pullbacks of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and at rational level their scalar localization as in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The geometric-point return means
$$
 g_Y^n\circ\bar x=\bar x\circ g_s^n,
$$
not the equality $g_Y^n\circ\bar x=\bar x$ of scheme morphisms: $\gamma^n$ fixes the subfield $\mathbf F_{q^n}$ [lem-weil-unique-subfield-of-closure]. Let $N=L\bar x^*M$ and form the map
$$
 I^{[n]}_N:\operatorname{Fib}_s(N)\longrightarrow
 \operatorname{Fib}_s(L(g_s^n)^*N)
$$
by composing the point transports $\iota_N,\iota_{Lg_s^*N},\ldots,\iota_{(Lg_s^*)^{n-1}N}$ of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] and the pullback-composition comparison. Define the local operator $F_x^{(n)}:C_{\bar x}\to C_{\bar x}$ to be the composite
$$
 C_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{I^{[n]}_N}
 \operatorname{Fib}_s(L(g_s^n)^*L\bar x^*M)
 \xrightarrow{\sim}
 \operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*L(g_Y^n)^*M)
 \xrightarrow{\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*\theta^{[n]})}C_{\bar x},
$$
where the middle isomorphism uses the displayed equality of scheme morphisms and the specified composition comparisons. Denote its induced operator on each $\mathrm H^j(C_{\bar x})$ by $F_x^{(n)}$ as well.

For a closed point $y\in|Y_0|$ [def-weil-closed-points], let $r=[\kappa(y):k_0]$, with residue field as in [def-weil-residue-field]; this is a finite positive degree by [lem-kun-closed-point-field](a). Choose a $k_0$-embedding $\kappa(y)\hookrightarrow k$ and the associated geometric point $\bar y:s\to Y$. Use the same construction with $n=r$ and the resulting return $g_Y^r\bar y=\bar y g_s^r$ to define $F_y$ on $\mathcal H^j(M)_{\bar y}$ for every $j\in\mathbf Z$.

Finally define the local alternating trace by
$$
 \operatorname{Tr}(F_x^{(n)}\mid K_{\bar x})
 :=\sum_{j\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^j
 \operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F_x^{(n)}\mid\mathcal H^j(M)_{\bar x}\bigr)\in E.
$$
Each summand uses the ordinary linear trace [def-weil-endomorphism-trace], and the sum is finite by the bounded finite-dimensional point-complex convention above. The analogous closed-point trace uses $F_y$ and $\bar y$.

proof.text: For localExtensionPoint_compatible, use the final choose_spec equality in exists_unique_subfield_of_closure: the extensionEmbedding followed by the subfield inclusion is algebraMap. Rewrite Over.w and contravariant Spec composition. For localClosedPoint_compatible, rewrite Scheme.Hom.specMap_residueFieldAlgebraMap and Spec composition, then use the given compatibility hι.

For localClosedPointDegree_pos, equip the actual residue field with the algebra structure from Y₀.hom.residueFieldAlgebraMap. The finite-residue-field equivalence of closedPoint_iff_residueField_trdeg_zero_and_finite gives Module.Finite. Module.finrank_pos gives degree at least one because a field is nontrivial.

Induct on the positive-power index to identify localPositivePower of frobeniusPointIso with Spec of the corresponding positive power of geometricFrobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic. Induct using galoisMap_projections to show that the model projection of localPositivePower of geometricFrobenius is unchanged, and its closure projection is followed by the same positive power of frobeniusPointIso. Pullback.hom_ext then proves the return equation for any lift whose model map is fixed by this point power.

For localExtensionPoint_return, choose_spec of exists_unique_subfield_of_closure gives cardinality q^n of extensionSubfield, hence finiteness. For localClosedPoint_return, the closed-point residue-field theorem gives Module.Finite; Module.finite_of_finite and Module.natCard_eq_pow_finrank give a finite field of cardinality q^r. In each case apply the existing proved source-library theorem FiniteField.geometricFrobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic_pow_apply_of_card_eq to the prescribed field embedding. Spec composition makes the model map fixed, so the lift calculation of the preceding step applies. The inequalities n>=1 and r>=1 identify (n-1)+1 and (r-1)+1 with n and r. The definitions of the local operators and traces are unchanged.

split_report.summary: Expanded the imported definition into explicit data: the iterated Weil isomorphism, geometric-point reparametrization, point-fiber transport and cohomological trace. Reused the existing finite-level pullback-composition and point-transport interfaces; the integral composition comparison for the pullbacks of def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom is the new statement-only node lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition (maintainer reader, 2026-10-17), replacing a citation of lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange, whose completed pullback is a different construction, and added the missing ordinary-trace and point-complex definitions. Removed the global cohomology-Frobenius dependency, whose separatedness hypothesis the local construction does not need, and replaced the scheme-property bundle by the exact definitions used. The Lean stalk and trace definitions only cover algebraically closed coefficients and omit the derived-stalk clause, so there is no full attachment. One new node, created at the maintainer review.
